question.worked_solution:
First, we find ${f}^{′}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t))\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{6}{t})\,k \\  & =(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t)+2)\,i-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j-\frac{6}{{t}^{2}}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, to compute ${f}^{′}(1),$ we substitute $t=1$ into the expression for ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1) & =(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot 1)+2)\,i-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)\,j-\frac{6}{{1}^{2}}\,k \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\,i-5\operatorname{cos}⁡1\,j-6\,k\end{aligned}
$$
